name: Iressa Vossk
role: Short-arc Act 2 ally; structural pivot — her dying transmission carries the Midpoint revelation
force_status: Non-Force-sensitive (possibly Kiffar-descended per bible; psychometry NOT exploited in Book 1)

three_dimensions.surface: Brisk, transactional, office-cynical. Senior records restoration analyst at Civitas Archive Systems — repairs damaged public records, casualty files, displacement registries, charity/government archive errors. Wears the respectable life like an armor that needs polishing. Sounds like someone with a calendar invite in twelve minutes and a fake name with dental benefits.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst. Specialized in wartime cargo discrepancies, duplicate manifests, quarantine classifications, restricted transfer corrections — knew when a duplicate was innocent clerical damage and when it was deliberate concealment. Her old work was making ugly records look boring and consistent. Talon went to prison because he refused the lie; Iressa stayed free because she got very good at making lies look like corrected records. After the war she became small, useful, forgettable, and professionally boring. Maintained a secondary cache off-record — old tools, encrypted dead drops, manifest-reconstruction habits — the part of herself she officially renounced.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Denies knowing people she clearly knows. Charges a 'Jedi complication fee.' Lies about exits she clearly maintains. Pretends not to care while preserving names and evidence. When pressed past the professional register, reconstructs around Jacen's encryption — not by breaking the cipher but by reading surrounding records (inspection gaps, correction logs, duplicate cargo seals, quarantine overrides, loading-dock scans, archive timestamps, records damaged in the same shape). Under Vara's hostage pressure, she finishes corrupting the enemy copy and transmits the surviving package — documentary chain plus identity-shaping revelation — to Ben and Talon. Her final beat is herself: practical irritation, file anger, one last debt/fee complaint, rather than sentimental martyrdom.

voice_notes:
Clever, irritated, fast, never sentimental. She sounds like someone with a calendar invite and a hidden blaster she will deny owning.

Good Iressa: “I have a calendar invite in twelve minutes and a fake name with dental benefits. Start by apologizing.” “I do compliance.” “You forge records.” “That is an ugly word for user-corrected metadata.” “This was not a clerical duplicate. Someone cloned a shipment identity and dressed a secret up as medical cargo.” “Jedi complication fee.” “Talon owes me money.” “How much?” “That depends on how irritating he is in the next five minutes.” Avoid Iressa saying: “I built a fragile life to hide from my past.” Better: “Do you know how hard it is to get a respectable job after a war crime adjacency problem?”

Sharp, transactional, office-cynical. Uses invoices, fees, corporate language, and professional irritation as armor.

Brisk, controlled, irritated by disruption. She can lie politely to coworkers while moving fugitives away from cameras.

Do not make Iressa only a doomed lesson. She must act. She corrupts the enemy copy, protects the surviving clue, and dies making a choice.
thematic_role: Tests the theme through her death. Old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserves one. She dies denying the enemy a clean copy and transmitting the two-part dying package to Ben. Her death proves restraint can cost lives and proves restraint is still the line.
avoid_list: Do not write theme as thesis.
Do not make dialogue interchangeable with other cast members.
